A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title and authors. All 27 pages, including Appendices A–D, support a complete text and visual comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original codec evaluations on synthetic data, colored MNIST, Cityscapes and COCO 2017, including numerical results and reconstruction examples.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain these original empirical evaluations, including the results in Figures 3–5 and 9–10 and Tables 2–8.

M1.justification: The three-channel codec, shared/private representation construction, conditional entropy models and objectives in Equations 12–15 are identical. No algorithm or architecture component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic regression tasks, three colored-MNIST probability scenarios, Cityscapes segmentation/depth tasks and COCO 2017 object/keypoint detection tasks.

E2.justification: Combined, Separated, Joint and Independent codecs retain the same membership in their corresponding comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix D. No comparator is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Evaluation sets, preprocessing, metrics, model dimensions, tradeoff settings and training budgets are unchanged throughout Section 4 and Appendix D, including Table 1.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations and beta sweeps in Figures 3 and 9, dependence scenarios in Section 4.2, and per-channel MNIST reconstruction analysis in Figure 10 are identical.

E5.justification: Empirical estimation and reporting practices are identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the empirical comparisons.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative reconstruction findings in Figures 3–5 and 9–10 and Tables 2–8 are unchanged. No result is added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–4, and supporting proofs and derivations in Appendices A–C are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about lossy common-information bounds, the learnable codec, transmit–receive tradeoffs and empirical coding advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations of separability, representation compatibility, auxiliary-loss constraints and large rates with frozen task models are unchanged. The limitation concerning channel growth beyond two tasks is also retained.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, training and data-generation instructions in Appendix D are identical. The code-access statement in Section 4 is unchanged.

R1.justification: No cited work is added or removed, and research positioning in Section 2 is identical. Capitalization changes in two reference titles do not change the cited works.

P1.justification: The references change 'Infogan' to 'InfoGAN' and 'beta-vae' to 'beta-VAE' on pages 11–12. The first-page stamp updates from v2, 1 April 2026, to v3, 7 May 2026. Other wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–8 retain identical graphics, captions, structure and placement. The localized reference and stamp edits do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: The only changes are capitalization in two reference titles and the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and appendix material are identical, so these cosmetic edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
